subject.title: feat(talk): use Codex OAuth for browser realtime voice

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a public realtime browser-session broker contract for the bundled Codex plugin, or keep Codex OAuth realtime voice outside the current Talk provider architecture?
rationale: The PR adds a new capability and Plugin SDK surface that affects future provider/plugin ownership; this is a durable product and compatibility decision, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor the broker contract
options.body: Approve the Codex-plugin broker direction after protocol review and require focused live browser/iOS evidence plus compatibility coverage before merge.

options.title: Keep the current Platform-only route
options.body: Decline the new OAuth fallback and retain existing Platform-key browser WebRTC behavior until a broader provider contract is designed.

options.title: Narrow to a private experiment
options.body: Ask for a smaller owner-plugin implementation that avoids exporting a general Plugin SDK broker contract until the API direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the broker contract
recommendation.body: Approve the Codex-plugin broker direction after protocol review and require focused live browser/iOS evidence plus compatibility coverage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the proposed implementation and can provide the technical design context, while the protected label requires maintainer sponsorship for the final product decision.
